purpose: Preserve the conceptual trajectory of the conversation, make the current frontier explicit, and test whether Inquiry Graph can represent the distinctions needed to resume and improve this inquiry.

findings.description: The frame seam has now been pressure-tested with a thin derived FrameProfile over three real graphs. The repeated cross-case invariant is smaller than originally feared: frame content, inquiry scope/applies-to, and active query. Method-specific coordinates such as model hypothesis, criterion, boundary/access, resources, and perspective remain optional. Framing/reframing acts and frame-relative candidate/question consequences stay in existing graph structures.
findings.current_workaround: Use the derived FrameProfile sidecar. Frame content, applies-to scope, and active query are required profile roles; method-specific coordinates remain optional references to existing graph objects.
findings.proposed_change: Keep Frame as a projection/profile rather than a core V1 node kind. Next test inter-reviewer agreement on frame identity/scope/query bindings and measure whether the profile improves resumption, motif mining, or candidate-generation analysis.
findings.promotion_gate: Only promote first-class frame semantics if independent reviewers materially disagree on the thin profile or a named downstream use cannot be served reliably by the projection.

findings.description: Recurring strategies or reasoning motifs are not first-class records. Current guidance represents a strategy as a method node and an occurrence as an example linked by part_of/exemplifies. This conversation makes motif analysis important, but does not yet show that the workaround loses a necessary query.
findings.current_workaround: Use method nodes for reusable strategies and example/part_of/exemplifies for grounded episodes.
findings.proposed_change: Evaluate motif queries over multiple conversations before considering StrategyEpisode or another core construct.
findings.promotion_gate: Show at least one material motif-analysis query that cannot be answered faithfully with method + example + part_of/exemplifies, and reproduce the failure across more than one conversation.

findings.description: This fixture is a curated excerpt map rather than a reconciled native transcript. That is adequate for the conceptual thread but weak for exhaustive move/motif mining and actor-level stance analysis.
findings.current_workaround: The conversation coverage note explicitly declares the limitation and no unobserved turns are inferred.
findings.proposed_change: When available, add a repeatable path from native conversation export to graph extraction and compare it with this curated fixture.
findings.promotion_gate: Obtain a stable native export/input path and show that the additional source fidelity changes or improves a concrete downstream use enough to justify the extraction cost.

findings.description: Inquiry Graph previously captured conversations without requiring a structured review of how well the representation served the inquiry. That loses evidence about recurring schema, extraction, and workflow friction.
findings.current_workaround: Ad hoc notes and conversation discussion.
findings.proposed_change: Adopt the sibling fit-review sidecar and documented conversation-to-graph self-improvement loop.
findings.promotion_gate: Merge this workflow only after the sidecar parses, the example graph validates, and the process explicitly prevents a single conversation from silently changing shared semantics.

findings.description: A self-improvement loop can conflate evidence of representational friction with authority to change the ontology. The conversation explicitly asks for improvement over time, but the repository must keep diagnosis, proposal, and semantic promotion separate.
findings.current_workaround: Human review and ordinary pull-request discipline.
findings.proposed_change: Make promotion gates mandatory in fit-review findings and state the rule 'self-improving, not self-authorizing' in the workflow.
findings.promotion_gate: Require every shared semantic change to cite its fit-review evidence, prior-art/reuse check, and regression evidence; no automatic schema mutation from fit-review output.

findings.description: The reuse-first landscape maps proactive question/frame exploration to mature owners: frame creation/reframing, Problem Structuring Methods, C-K concept/knowledge co-expansion, literature-based discovery, transformational creativity, and metareasoning. The gap is now integration and empirical usefulness, not absence of theory.
findings.current_workaround: Use method nodes and the existing generative-system transformation interface to represent concrete framing/question-exploration methods while keeping active frame/scope as a derived profile.
findings.proposed_change: Do not add a universal unknown-unknown or frame-shift primitive. Run a real parallel workflow test combining reuse/discovery search with frame/question exploration and measure whether it finds better prior art, shrinks residual invention, or improves downstream decisions.
findings.promotion_gate: Only promote new shared semantics if the parallel workflow reveals a repeated representational failure that mature method-specific owners plus the existing Frame profile/generative-regime interface cannot express.

findings.description: The first parallel-inquiry pilot produced positive but weak process evidence. A reuse/discovery lane found an existing Epistemic Warrant participant-relative frame factorization that the earlier sequential frame discussion had not surfaced; an empirical frame/question lane independently identified only three repeated cross-case needs. Integrating the lanes reduced the proposed abstraction to a thin profile rather than expanding it.
findings.current_workaround: Use lane separation by source/task role inside one research session: empirical/problem-pressure lane plus reuse/prior-art lane, followed by residual-minimizing integration.
findings.proposed_change: Retain the parallel pattern as a workflow hypothesis and repeat it on at least one materially different inquiry with more controlled lane isolation/budget before promoting it as general agent orchestration doctrine.
findings.promotion_gate: Require a second materially different case and, where feasible, independent lane execution or fixed budgets showing improved prior-art recovery, smaller residual invention, or better downstream decisions.

findings.description: The conversation sharpens reuse-before-invention into an asymmetric control policy: apparent novelty itself should increase search pressure and trigger attempts to falsify novelty before bespoke invention is authorized. Inquiry Graph can record this as a method/goal, but the broader agent workflow does not yet carry an explicit novelty-escalation discipline.
findings.current_workaround: Rely on general reuse-first guidance and human correction when agents positively frame apparent novelty.
findings.proposed_change: Adopt an explicit novelty-falsification/search-escalation policy in agent engineering guidance: apparent novelty raises the burden of search, terminology translation, adjacent-domain review, composition attempts, failed-attempt review, and requirement/frame challenge before residual invention.
findings.promotion_gate: Operationalize first as workflow/planning guidance and test on concrete engineering plans. Do not turn it into a semantic primitive unless repeated cross-domain use requires one.

overall_assessment: The first comparative workflow pilot supports both current directions without earning new ontology. A thin FrameProfile over three real graphs needs only content, applies-to scope, and active query as cross-case invariants; optional coordinates reuse existing Epistemic Warrant distinctions. The parallel empirical + reuse/discovery workflow also found an internal prior-art owner missed by the earlier sequential discussion and materially reduced residual invention, but the evidence is one-session and not controlled.
next_inquiry_question: Do independent reviewers agree on the thin FrameProfile bindings, and does the parallel empirical + reuse/discovery pattern reproduce its residual-invention reduction on a second materially different inquiry?
